findings.text: She turned back up the lane toward the dark houses with the light held low against her thigh, hearing them come after her.
findings.deletionTest: She turned back up the lane toward the dark houses with the light held low against her thigh, and they came after her.
findings.issue: The filter verb routes the rangers' following through Sylvanas's ears. Nothing depends on how she perceives it here (unlike L810, where hearing the empty road behind her is the beat), so the deletion test passes.
findings.suggestedFix: She turned back up the lane toward the dark houses with the light held low against her thigh, and her rangers fell in behind her.

findings.text: The girl shook her head against Neral's collar, and Neral did not ask again.
findings.issue: This is the second non-action beat in the end-house/cellar scene. The strongest is L372 'Neral did not touch the ring.', where the scene turns on the restraint. Under F12, every non-action beat after the strongest one in a scene is a KILL. A positive verb can carry the same gentleness.
findings.suggestedFix: The girl shook her head against Neral's collar, and Neral let the name go.

findings.text: In anyone else she would have called that very convenient.
findings.couldEndEarlierAt: She had kept the mage because the mage was a prisoner, and you did not hand a Kirin Tor apprentice to a relay rider with a child on her saddle.
findings.issue: Sylvanas asks herself a question, gives a flat 'No.' and an over-built reason. The reader can already see that the reason is a rationalisation. The closer then names that irony outright and finishes the thought for the reader. The voice sheet says her humour is 'deadpan and never underlined' and that she 'declines to sort out' whether she trusts the mage or only her results. This line underlines the joke and does the sorting. Without it, the next paragraph ('Both.' about the child) contrasts better with the 'No.'
findings.fixAction: delete sentence; paragraph ends on '...with a child on her saddle.'

audits.registerSummary: Ranger-General, tracker and field commander. She thinks in ground, sign, sightlines and drills, and checks every inference against her own tracking experience. Her inner voice argues with itself in short self-orders ('Don't.', 'Open the doors.', 'Leave it.') and sardonic asides, and she swears by the sun. Her humour is deadpan and never underlined. She would not think in narrative or thematic terms, predict her own memory, or narrate outcomes before they happen.

findings.text: Neral found it in the end house.
findings.whoIsSayingThis: A narrator. The line announces the outcome of the search before the scene happens, then the next paragraph rewinds to Sylvanas up a ladder next door.
findings.povMismatch: In the moment Sylvanas does not know anyone will find anything. The summary is told from after the scene, which breaks Limited Third Absolute and spends the suspense of the search. 'It' is also a placeholder for the hatch or the child, neither of which is on the page yet.
findings.fixAction: delete sentence; scene opens on 'The end house stood where the garden walls gave out, its back wall right on the lane.'

findings.text: It was a face she would forget in any crowd: weathered, stubbled grey, a nose broken once and set crooked.
findings.whoIsSayingThis: A narrator. The line predicts what Sylvanas will later fail to remember. It is the mirror of the guide's calibration KILL 'She would remember this later.'
findings.povMismatch: The line labels the carter 'forgettable' instead of letting him read that way. The plan says the clue must be 'visible on the page but not signposted' and that Sylvanas builds no case around him. Telling the reader he is forgettable is a signpost. The label also clashes with the detail after it (a crooked, broken nose is the most memorable thing in the description).
findings.suggestedFix: A weathered face, stubbled grey, the nose broken once and set crooked.
